strengths: Comprehensive theoretical analysis under both standard Lipschitz smooth and generalized (L₀,L₁)-smooth conditions with four convergence theorems achieving O(ε⁻³) sample complexity
Practical memory improvement from O(mn) to O((m+n)r̂) by combining variance-reduced momentum with randomized SVD
Batch size 1 efficiency throughout training, unlike Muon++ requiring batch size O(ε⁻¹)
Addresses realistic smoothness conditions in deep learning rather than strict Lipschitz smoothness
Well-structured comparison table (Table 1) positioning the work relative to recent Muon variants
weaknesses: Critically weak experimental validation: only 5,000 training iterations (far too short), and Option #2 (the main contribution) significantly underperforms Option #1 on both tasks (DistilGPT2: 346.41 vs 170.34 validation PPL; ViT: 23.61% vs 26.59% accuracy), undermining practical utility

Assumption 5 is restrictive and poorly justified: requires tail singular values bounded by gradient norm but provides no empirical evidence this holds during neural network training or analysis of robustness to violations
Limited technical novelty: straightforward combination of existing techniques (STORM momentum + randomized SVD) without significant algorithmic innovation; O(ε⁻³) complexity matches existing Muon++

Significant theory-practice gap: RSVD approximation error not fully integrated into convergence proofs; theoretical convergence to stationarity not validated in short experiments that don't reach convergence

Inadequate experimental rigor: no statistical measures (error bars, multiple runs), no wall-clock time comparisons, no ablation studies, hyperparameter fairness unclear, tested only on small models (22-82M parameters) with insufficient iterations

strengths: Solid theoretical contributions with comprehensive convergence analysis under multiple settings (exact SVD vs Newton-Schulz, Lipschitz vs generalized smoothness)
Novel combination of variance reduction (STORM) and randomized SVD for Muon optimizer
Addresses dual objectives: simultaneous memory reduction and improved sample complexity
Broad empirical evaluation across diverse architectures (Mamba, Qwen, ViT)
Detailed proofs in appendix demonstrating technical rigor
weaknesses: Significant gap between theory (exact SVD) and practice (randomized SVD with rank truncation) - theoretical guarantees don't directly apply to Algorithm 1 as implemented
Inconsistent experimental results: full-rank LiMuon underperforms Muon on Mamba-130M (47.78 vs 47.08 validation); improvements marginal and architecture-dependent
Practical improvements are modest: only 8-15% memory reduction (22.2GB→20.25GB), but runtime per-step increases by ~5-15% and total training time sometimes slower

Sample complexity improvement O(ε⁻³) vs O(ε⁻⁴) is claimed but misleading - constants matter in practice, and RSVD overhead may negate theoretical gains; Newton-Schulz result shows χq³ vs χq⁴ dependency
Generalized smoothness assumption (4.4) is restrictive and not verified to hold for modern neural networks; clarity on when this assumption is reasonable is lacking
Missing ablation studies: no separate analysis of variance reduction vs RSVD contributions; sensitivity to rank selection not studied
Incomplete experimental analysis: unclear if all methods received equal hyperparameter tuning effort; no error bars or multiple runs; comparison with SUMO (memory-reducing baseline) is limited
Theory-practice gap not adequately addressed: approximation error accumulation from RSVD over iterations not analyzed; practical algorithm constants could be large
